capabilities: Manage a shared endpoint list with protocols, capabilities, default models and on/off switches
Store API tokens in Obsidian's keychain instead of data.json
Check endpoint reachability and report status with reasons
Detect backend server software such as LM Studio, Ollama and Open WebUI
Expose an API that lets other plugins resolve endpoints by capability
extras: Not reviewed by Obsidian staff. Requires Obsidian 1.11.4+ because tokens use the keychain. The README documents a trust-model warning: any installed plugin can call the API and receive a token, and caller names are self-declared. Full documentation, getting-started and troubleshooting pages live outside the README.
problem: Multiple AI plugins in a vault each ask separately for the same server addresses and API tokens, with no shared place to configure or store them.

relations.evidence: lingotuner (since 0.10.0) and Koda (since 0.28.0) can use it already
lingotuner (since 0.10.0) and Koda (since 0.28.0) can use it already

requires.name: a reachable model server such as LM Studio, Ollama or a hosted OpenAI-compatible API
at least one plugin that consumes the endpoint API
API token for hosted endpoints such as Anthropic's Claude API

summary: Central manager for LLM endpoint configurations (URLs, protocols, models, capabilities) with API tokens kept in Obsidian's keychain, shared with other plugins through an API.
